newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The fifth round of talks between the government and the tribal Shanti Bahini rebels begin in Dhaka on Monday.
The government has asked for technical assistance from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank to strengthen the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
Sixteen more people were reported dead on Sunday, raising the death toll to 72 in the current flooding that washed a bridge, roads and caused extensive damage to crops.

Nearly 300 workers of a Korean industrial unit in the Dhaka Export Processing Zone (DEPZ) were injured in police assult on Thursday while agitating for the release of two of their fellow workers from police custody.
Former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad, released from jail early this year, leaves Dhaka for Saudi Arabia for treatment.
The authorities has decided to airdrop relief materials and dry food in remote flood-hit areas.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria on Sunday said banks had been asked to file cases against loan defaulters.
Work at the Chittagong Port will continue round the clock for one month since July 13. REUTER
